title: Case File Summarisation and Chronology
summary: Turn a litigation file of pleadings, affidavits, exhibits and orders into an indexed list of dates and events, a party and witness index and issue summaries, each line linked to its page.

seo.title: Case File Summarisation and Chronology with AI | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that indexes litigation files, builds a list of dates and events with page citations and drafts issue-wise summaries for counsel to verify.

problem.intro: A commercial suit, arbitration or writ petition can arrive with thousands of pages: plaint, written statement, replication, affidavits of evidence, exhibits, correspondence and years of interim orders, often scanned, sometimes in Hindi, with handwritten order sheets from the district court. Before any strategy work, someone has to read it all and build the chronology.

pain_points.title: Chronologies built by hand
pain_points.detail: Associates spend days preparing the list of dates and events, and it goes stale the moment a new affidavit is filed.

pain_points.title: Facts without sources
pain_points.detail: Summaries that do not cite pages are hard to rely on when preparing for a hearing or a cross-examination.

pain_points.title: Contradictions are missed
pain_points.detail: Dates, amounts and statements that differ between pleadings, affidavits and documents are easy to overlook in a large file.

pain_points.title: Mixed scripts and poor scans
pain_points.detail: Hindi orders, handwritten notings and low-quality photocopies defeat standard search.

solution.overview: We build a case-file assistant that ingests the paper book or matter folder, runs OCR in English and Hindi, classifies each document and indexes it by type, date and filing party. It extracts dated events, amounts, parties and witnesses and builds a list of dates and events in which every entry cites the document and page. Issue-wise summaries are drafted from the pleadings and evidence, and possible contradictions are listed for counsel, such as a date in the plaint that differs from an exhibit. Associates verify entries against the source in one click, and the chronology updates when new documents are added.
capabilities: OCR for English and Hindi, including handwritten order sheets, with low-confidence text marked
Document index by type, date, filing party and exhibit number
List of dates and events with a document and page citation for every entry
Party, witness and entity index across the file
Issue-wise summaries drawn from the pleadings and evidence
Contradiction list across pleadings, affidavits and exhibits for counsel to assess

workflow.title: Load the file
workflow.detail: The paper book, matter folder or court-downloaded documents are uploaded for the matter.

workflow.title: OCR and classify
workflow.detail: Each document is read and classified as plaint, reply, affidavit, exhibit, order and so on.

workflow.title: Extract events and entities
workflow.detail: Dates, events, amounts, parties and witnesses are extracted with page references.

workflow.title: Build the chronology
workflow.detail: Events are ordered into a list of dates and events, and conflicting dates are flagged.

workflow.title: Associate verification
workflow.detail: An associate checks flagged entries, and a sample of the others, against the source pages.

workflow.title: Export and update
workflow.detail: The verified chronology, index and summaries are exported to Word and refreshed as new filings arrive.

inputs: Pleadings: plaint or petition, written statement, replication and rejoinder
Affidavits of evidence and witness statements
Matter details: parties, court and case number
outputs: Document index with type, date and filing party
List of dates and events with page citations
human_in_the_loop: Associates verify every flagged entry, and a sample of the rest, before the chronology is used, and counsel decide what any contradiction means for the case. Summaries are working notes for lawyers, not opinions.
guardrails: Every chronology entry cites a document and page
Contradictions presented as questions for counsel, not conclusions
Matter-level access controls with no cross-matter retrieval
Documents not used to train models
compliance_notes: Case files contain personal and sometimes sensitive data of parties and witnesses; designed to support DPDP Act 2023 safeguards.
Internal notes and drafts are stored separately from the evidence index to help protect privileged work.

pilot.scope: Two or three closed or consented matters of different sizes, with chronologies compared against ones your team has already prepared.
deliverables: Document types and chronology format agreed with your litigation team
Indexed files and chronologies for the pilot matters
Comparison report against your existing chronologies

faqs.q: Can it read handwritten district court order sheets?
faqs.a: Often, but not always. Handwritten notings are read where legible and marked with lower confidence; illegible pages are flagged so an associate can transcribe them.

faqs.q: Is the summary a legal opinion?
faqs.a: No. It is a working summary of what the documents say, with citations, to help counsel prepare. Analysis and advice stay with the lawyers.

faqs.q: How do we handle new filings mid-case?
faqs.a: Add them to the matter folder. The index, chronology and contradiction list are updated, and changes since the last version are highlighted.
In your environment or a chosen India region, with access restricted to the matter team. Models do not train on your files.
